sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! After pressing LEFT:
- The green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] didn't move (still at same position)
- But the green square INSIDE the left frame moved! It went from [[33, 12], [33, 14], [35, 14], [35, 12]] to [[33, 9], [33, 11], [35, 11], [35, 9]]
- The left frame changed shape: boundary is now [[32, 11], [32, 15], [36, 15], [36, 11], [36, 14], [35, 15], [33, 15], [32, 14]] - it seems damaged again
So pressing LEFT moves the green square inside the frame, not the one outside! This is different from before.
Wait, actually, let me reconsider. Previously, when I pressed LEFT, the green square at [[30, 18], [30, 20], [32, 20], [32, 18]] moved to [[30, 15], [30, 17], [32, 17], [32, 15]]. Now the green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] didn't move, but the one inside the frame did.
So it seems like the arrow keys control the green square that's NOT inside a frame. But now the green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] is not inside a frame, and it didn't move. Instead, the one inside the frame moved.
Wait, that's contradictory. Let me think again. Maybe the arrow keys control the "active" green square, which is the one that was most recently moved or interacted with. Or maybe there's a different rule.
Actually, looking more carefully:
- Before LEFT: green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] with charcoal center, green square at [[33, 12], [33, 14], [35, 14], [35, 12]] with white center
- After LEFT: green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] with charcoal center (same position), green square at [[33, 9], [33, 11], [35, 11], [35, 9]] with white center (moved left)
So the green square inside the frame moved left, exiting the frame. The frame was damaged in the process.
This suggests that arrow keys move ALL green squares, or the one that can move in that direction. Or maybe the arrow keys move the green square that's not blocked.
Wait, but the green square at [[30, 30], [30, 32], [32, 32], [32, 30]] is adjacent to the purple bar on its right. If I press LEFT, it should move left. But it didn't. Instead, the other green square moved.
Hmm, maybe the rule is that arrow keys move the green square that's inside a frame (or was inside a frame). Or maybe there's a selection mechanism I'm not seeing.
Actually, let me reconsider. In the initial state, there were two green squares outside frames and a white square. When I pressed LEFT initially, one green square moved left. Now, after many actions, pressing LEFT moves a different green square.
Let me try pressing RIGHT to see what happens.
Actually, I notice something important. The green square that moved is the one with the WHITE center. Maybe the arrow keys always control the green square with the white center (or some other distinguishing feature).
Let me check: in the initial state, the green square with the WHITE center was at [[30, 18], [30, 20], [32, 20], [32, 18]]. When I pressed LEFT, it moved to [[30, 15], [30, 17], [32, 17], [32, 15]]. So yes, the arrow keys control the green square with the white center.
Now, after swapping centers, the green square with the white center is at [[33, 12], [33, 14], [35, 14], [35, 12]] (inside the left frame). When I pressed LEFT, it moved to [[33, 9], [33, 11], [35, 11], [35, 9]].
So the arrow keys control the green square with the WHITE center. This is the key insight!
Now, the goal might be to:
1. Get the green square with the white center into a specific position
2. Or get both green squares into their respective frames with the correct center colors
Let me think about what the correct configuration might be. The left frame and right frame each have a 3x3 interior. Maybe the goal is to have:
- A green square with a white center in the left frame
- A green square with a black/charcoal center in the right frame
But the purple bar blocks access to the right frame. Unless... the purple bar can be removed or bypassed.
Wait, let me look at the ascii again. The green square with the white center is now at [[33, 9], [33, 11], [35, 11], [35, 9]], which is outside the left frame. The left frame is at [[32, 11], [32, 15], [36, 15], [36, 11]].
Let me try to move the green square with the white center back into the left frame by pressing RIGHT.

# The arrow keys control the green square with the WHITE center.

result = action(['RIGHT'])
seg = current_frame.segmentation
print("After RIGHT:")
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] in ['N', 'c', 'W', 'B'] and n['pixels'] <= 20:
        print(f"  color={n['color']} pixels={n['pixels']} boundary={n['boundary']}")
print("Level completed:", last_action_result.get('level_completed'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
